clue.text: Brief edition with coverage of tidings from the east country

indicators.note: the reversed word gives cover to, i.e. wraps around, the short edition
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: tidings are news
ED is the standard short form of edition

explanation.surface: A short newspaper edition carrying reports from eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'from the east' means reading right to left, giving SWEN; 'coverage of' has that wrap the short edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: It may describe one who has been singularly successful

definitions.text: It may describe one who has been singularly successful

parts.words: It may describe one who has been singularly successful
parts.note: singularly hints at success achieved by oneself alone, without help from others

explanation.surface: A description fitting someone remarkably successful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singularly' seems to mean 'remarkably', but it means 'by a single person', someone who built their own fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rose by their own efforts without inheritance or patronage is described with this compound adjective.

clue.text: Was coach learned?

definitions.meaning: coached, trained or taught someone, in the past tense

explanation.surface: Asking whether the trainer had any schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of a verb for teaching, and also an adjective for being well schooled.

clue.text: Treatment for ache in a head

indicators.note: treatment of the letters works them over into a new order

explanation.surface: A remedy for a pain in someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' looks like part of the medical picture but means 'per person', as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Per person: 'a head' and this word both mean for every individual.

clue.text: It's impressive-looking, but it's not working

explanation.surface: Something looks impressive, yet it does not function.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means eye-catching, and also refers to workers taking industrial action.

clue.text: Complete meals for the road

parts.note: thorough means complete, utter
fare is food, the meals served

explanation.surface: Full meals to take on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A main public street or route is a synonym for a road.

clue.text: Stops for refreshment in Nova Scotia

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for the Canadian province of Nova Scotia

explanation.surface: Places to pause for food and drink while travelling in Nova Scotia.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs and hostelries are places where travellers stop to eat and drink.

clue.text: Naughty ladies which men dream of

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Racy women who feature in men's fantasies.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect standards or goals are what people aspire to and dream about.

clue.text: Fuel that man would cut

parts.note: gas is a fuel
he'd is the contraction of 'he would', with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man who would cut off the fuel supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Slashed or wounded with a long deep cut, past tense.

clue.text: Start off with a meal outside

indicators.note: the meal sits outside the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: lunch is a meal

explanation.surface: Beginning the day with food served outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something going or begin it, as with a new product or project.

clue.text: Goes down as original organisers

definitions.meaning: the people who first set up an institution

explanation.surface: The organisers who started things are going under.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for a ship sinking, and a noun for those who establish a company or society.

clue.text: High court official

parts.note: the high chair at a tennis court seats the person who rules on play

explanation.surface: A senior official of the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High court' suggests a senior law court, but it is a tennis court, where this official sits up high.
explanation.definitionFit: The person seated in a tall chair to rule on line calls and scoring in a tennis match.

clue.text: Aim, when near

definitions.meaning: intend, as in 'I aim to go'
stingy, a dated sense of near

explanation.surface: Asking about aiming when close to a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is an old word for tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means intend, and also miserly or stingy.

clue.text: Bawl half-heartedly downstairs

indicators.note: half of the doubled middle letters, the heart of the word, is dropped

parts.note: to bellow is to bawl or roar

explanation.surface: Someone shouting without much conviction from the floor beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Ls of BELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath, on a lower floor, as in 'the flat below'.

clue.text: Joy, for example, over capturing the French

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation captures, i.e. holds inside it, the French article
over means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: le is the French masculine for 'the'

explanation.surface: Delight, say, at catching the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives GE; 'capturing' has it hold the French article. 'for example' looks like a pointer to the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Great delight or merriment is a synonym for joy.

clue.text: Moving a jug

parts.note: jug and stir are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: Carrying a jug from one place to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is not a pitcher but slang for prison, as is 'stir'.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and about, in motion or activity.

clue.text: Now so upset as to faint

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: So distressed right now that one may pass out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose consciousness briefly, a synonym for faint as a verb.

clue.text: Designs wrong sort of robe

indicators.note: a sort of the letters means they are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A garment whose designs are all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'sort of' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn over nightclothes is a kind of robe.

clue.text: Secretary's boss can be a tyrant

definitions.meaning: the person who dictates letters for a secretary to take down

explanation.surface: An office manager who bullies their secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who dictates letters, and also an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: In time, giver suffers torment

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: the word giver suffers, being mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Eventually a donor goes through anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' makes GRIEV; 'In' places it within the word for a long period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress or trouble someone, close in sense to tormenting them.

clue.text: New Year activity with original basis

parts.note: first means original, earliest
a footing is a basis or foundation

explanation.surface: A seasonal pursuit with a new foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and northern England, being the first visitor across the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve is a custom bringing luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hogmanay custom of being the first guest to enter a house in January.

clue.text: Shower season

definitions.meaning: to pelt or shower with missiles

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to spray with shot, and also to spice food.

clue.text: You once turned in a spy on the other side

indicators.note: the turned-round pronoun goes in the spy's name

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional spy

indicators.note: turned means the old pronoun is reversed

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: A former spy who defected to the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes EY from the archaic pronoun; 'in' places it within the fictional agent's surname. 'turned' also plays on a spy changing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Farther than, across or past something, as with lands across a frontier.

clue.text: They look and sound agreeable

indicators.note: the word for agreement votes is said out loud

parts.note: ayes are votes in favour, people agreeing

explanation.surface: Some people seem and sound pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' and 'sound' read as a pair of verbs, but 'sound' signals a homophone of AYES.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are the parts of the body that look.

clue.text: Kind of public transport coming back into fashion?

indicators.note: coming back means the vehicles are read backwards

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Wondering whether trams are becoming fashionable again.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well dressed or chic means being in style, keen on what is current.

clue.text: Highlight of the show?

parts.note: highlight suggests both the best moment and the lead performer under the spotlight

explanation.surface: Asking about the best part of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading performer is the main attraction of any production.

clue.text: Fortune pocketed by Disraeli Parliament upheld

indicators.note: upheld says the hidden letters are read backwards
pocketed by says the letters are held inside the two names

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Riches pocketed by a Victorian prime minister's Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Fortune pocketed' as the definition, but 'pocketed by' signals the hidden word. In a down clue 'upheld' reverses ELIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is informal for a large amount of money, a fortune.

clue.text: Mad kind of motive?

definitions.meaning: the short word that, put before motive, makes the steam engine

explanation.surface: Asking whether some reason for acting is insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crazy, and also a prefix-like short form making a railway engine word.

clue.text: Being fertile for most of one's existence, I should reach 100

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: life is existence
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Remaining productive through a long life, nearly to a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing offspring or work in abundance, so highly fruitful.

clue.text: Group that is to make attack

parts.note: a sort is a group or kind
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A band of people preparing to launch an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sally out by troops from a defended position is an attack.

clue.text: Journalist following Marxist study became embarrassed

indicators.note: the journalist follows the other pieces, so comes last

parts.note: red is slang for a communist
a den is a private study
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter blushed after reading up on Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned red in the face from shame or self-consciousness, i.e. blushed.

clue.text: Pursue programme of studies

definitions.meaning: to chase game with hounds, as in hare coursing

explanation.surface: Following a plan of education.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for hunting with dogs, and a noun for a series of lectures or classes.
